introduction: A read-only browser interface: a landing page, a sign-in that does not disturb the person's API keys, a dashboard of their workspaces and a view of one workspace's state. It reads through the service's own API with the person's session, so the access rules already specified are the only ones.

glossary.browser session: What a person holds after signing in through the web interface. It identifies the same user an API credential would, but is not an API key and neither issues nor revokes one.
glossary.dashboard: The page listing the signed-in person's workspaces with their status and access.
glossary.visual language: The density, type scale, spacing, status colours and component patterns the interface borrows from GitHub and GitHub Copilot, under Parley's own name and marks.
glossary.workspace view: The page showing one workspace's state, its patches where it carries them, its recent jobs and its recent events.

requirements.title: The landing page
requirements.rationale: It is the only page an unauthenticated visitor sees, so it is also the page that must disclose nothing about the deployment.

criteria.condition: a visitor who is not signed in opens the service's root page
criteria.action: describe what the service is and what it does, and offer sign-in
criteria.contract: the page is served with a success status, carries a description of the service and a sign-in control, and does not redirect to an error

criteria.action: disclose nothing of the deployment's contents to a visitor who is not signed in
criteria.contract: no page served to an unauthenticated visitor contains a workspace slug, a user name, an organization name or any count of them

requirements.title: Signing in
requirements.rationale: The API's sign-in revokes every existing key of the user, so a browser that shared it would make opening the dashboard destructive.

criteria.condition: a visitor signs in through the web interface with the configured OAuth provider
criteria.action: establish a browser session identifying the same user the API would
criteria.contract: the session identifies the user the provider authenticated; the dashboard afterwards shows that user's workspaces

criteria.action: neither issue nor revoke an API key when a person signs in
criteria.contract: an API key held before a browser sign-in is accepted by the API after it; no new API key is created by signing in; the user's key list is unchanged

criteria.action: carry the session so that another site cannot make a request with it, expire it, and end it when the person signs out
criteria.contract: a cross-site request carrying no deliberate credential is not served as that person; an expired session is not accepted; after signing out the same session value is refused

criteria.condition: a visitor with no session, or one whose session has expired or been signed out, opens a page behind sign-in
criteria.action: show the landing page rather than an error
criteria.contract: the visitor is taken to the landing page with its sign-in control; no error page and no stack trace is shown

requirements.title: The dashboard
requirements.rationale: It is the first thing a person sees after signing in, and the place a leak of someone else's workspace would show.

criteria.condition: a signed-in person opens the dashboard
criteria.action: list their workspaces with each one's slug, status, their access to it and when it last synced, each linking to its own view
criteria.contract: every workspace the API would list for that person appears once, with those four fields shown and a working link to its view

criteria.action: list exactly the workspaces the same person's credential is given by the API, and no others
criteria.contract: the set of slugs shown equals the set the API returns for that person; a workspace of another user or organization never appears

criteria.condition: the signed-in person has no workspaces
criteria.action: say so and suggest what to do next
criteria.contract: the page carries a message explaining that there are no workspaces yet, rather than an empty list with no explanation

requirements.title: The workspace view
requirements.rationale: This is the page the whole feature exists for: enough to tell whether a workspace is healthy without running a command.

criteria.condition: a signed-in person opens a workspace they may read
criteria.action: show the workspace's slug, display name, description, status, mode, head, upstream head, last sync, any clone or sync error, and its settings
criteria.contract: each of those fields is shown with the value the API reports; an error field is shown when it is set and omitted when it is null

criteria.condition: the workspace being viewed carries patches
criteria.action: show the patch list in position order with each patch's position, branch, status and latest rebuild result, and show the latest rebuild
criteria.contract: the patches appear in ascending position order with those four fields; the latest rebuild's status is shown, or a statement that none has run; a standard workspace shows no patch section

criteria.action: show the workspace's most recent jobs and its most recent audit events
criteria.contract: the most recent jobs and events the API returns for that workspace are shown, newest first, each with its kind and time

criteria.condition: one section of the workspace view cannot be read
criteria.action: show the rest of the page and say which part could not be read
criteria.contract: the other sections render with their data; the failing section carries a message naming what could not be read; the page does not fail as a whole

requirements.title: Reading only what the person may
requirements.rationale: A second read path into the store would be a second place for the member, archived and bound-token rules to be got wrong.

criteria.action: make every read through the service's own API, as the signed-in person, rather than through a private path into the store
criteria.contract: every datum shown corresponds to a response the same person's session is entitled to; no page reads the relational store or the repository store directly

criteria.condition: a signed-in person opens the address of a workspace they may not read
criteria.action: show that it is not available, disclosing nothing about it
criteria.contract: the page says the workspace is not available and shows none of its fields; the answer is the same for a workspace that exists and one that does not

criteria.action: show a member of a workspace's organization exactly what the API gives a member
criteria.contract: a member's workspace view shows the fields the API returns them and omits every section the API would refuse them

requirements.title: How it looks and how it is used
requirements.rationale: The interface is for people, and a page that is unreadable in dark mode, unusable on a phone or unreachable by keyboard fails them regardless of its data.

criteria.action: follow the visual language of GitHub and GitHub Copilot in its density, type scale, spacing, status colours and its patterns for a repository list, a status badge and a timeline
criteria.contract: the dashboard uses the repository-list pattern, a workspace's status uses the status-badge pattern, and the events use the timeline pattern, each with the type scale and spacing the project's design tokens define once and reuse

criteria.action: provide a dark and a light theme following the viewer's system setting and overridable by the viewer
criteria.contract: every page renders in both themes; the theme follows the system setting by default and an explicit choice is remembered; every pair of text and background colour meets the contrast level for normal text in both themes

criteria.action: render every page usably at a phone's width
criteria.contract: at a viewport 360 pixels wide, every page renders with no horizontal scrolling and no content clipped or overlapping

criteria.action: make every interactive element reachable and operable from the keyboard, and give each page one main landmark, a heading structure with no skipped level and an accessible name for every control
criteria.contract: every link, button and control is reachable by keyboard in a sensible order, has a visible focus indicator and can be activated from the keyboard; each page has one main landmark, a heading structure with no skipped level, and an accessible name for every control

criteria.action: carry Parley's own name and marks and never present itself as GitHub or imply an association with it
criteria.contract: every page carries Parley's name; no page carries GitHub's name, logo or wordmark as its own identity, and none claims or implies an association

execution_paths.title: A developer signs in and their agent keeps running

steps.action: opens the landing page and chooses to sign in
authenticates the developer and returns them to the service
establishes a browser session without issuing or revoking an API key
reads the person's workspaces through the service's own API and shows the dashboard
makes a request with the API key it held throughout and is still served

execution_paths.title: A developer reads a patch stack's health in the browser

steps.action: opens a carry_patch workspace from the dashboard
reads the workspace, its patches, its latest rebuild, its recent jobs and its recent events through the API as that person
answers each read under the person's own access
sees the workspace's state, each patch with its latest rebuild result, the latest rebuild and the recent events on one page

execution_paths.title: A member sees their organization's workspaces and nothing else

steps.action: signs in and opens the dashboard
lists the workspaces the API gives that person, their organization's among them
opens one of the organization's workspaces and is shown the member's view
types the address of a workspace they may not read and is told it is not available, with none of its fields shown
